(4) Replaced karr_dna_damage_rng.py's disclosed `randsample_without_replacement` APPROXIMATION (randperm(n)[:k] for every (n,k)) with the EXACT real-MATLAB algorithm read directly from toolbox/stats/stats/randsample.m (4*k>n prefix-of-randperm branch; 4*k<=n rejection-sampling-over-builtin-randi branch), verified live against 6 real-MATLAB cases spanning both branches including a realistic genome-scale n=50000 rejection case (tests/vivarium/test_karr_dna_damage_rng.py, 32/32 passing) -- this ALSO fixed a genuine methodological trap hit mid-session: an early probe run shadowed the real toolbox randsample.m with this repo's OWN scripts/matlab/randsample.m fallback shim (a structurally different weighted-cdf algorithm), because MATLAB's `run()` changes cwd to the invoked script's own directory, silently defeating karr_bootstrap.m's own-directory re-shadow guard when the scratch script itself lived under scripts/matlab/ -- corrected by moving scratch invocations to a non-shadowing directory; all reported randsample ground truth was re-captured after the fix. replay_evidence.note_full_tick4_closure_2026_09_05: TICK-4 SINGLE-DRAW CLOSURE (2026-09-05, same branch): isolated and fixed the exact remaining draw from note_chromosome_ledger_fix_2026_09_04 above via per-reaction-granularity instrumentation, NOT inference from the aggregate 44/45. Built two hash-bound, per-reaction instrumented ledgers for seed2000 tick 5 (1-based; absolute tick 4, 0-based) and diffed them reaction-by-reaction: (1) scripts/matlab/instrument_dnadamage_tick4_per_reaction.m -- calls the REAL, unmodified DNADamage.m/Chromosome.m/RandStream.m methods externally (no source patch, no overlay of its own; only OBSERVES chromosome.randStream.state before/after each of tick 5's 32 real setSiteDamaged() calls via the same non-destructive clone-and-step reconstruction already used for the ledger), replaying ticks 1-4 with the extractor's own exact scheduler/allocation loop (copied verbatim, not refactored) to reach the identical real simulation state our trace was captured from -- independently confirmed via an exact match of chromosome.randStream.state entering tick 5 (1550145208.0, matching the already-captured ledger's tick-5 state_before to the last decimal). Source/provider hashes recorded (DNADamage.m/Chromosome.m/RandStream.m sha256, mnrnd/randsample/etc. toolbox provider identity) for exact provenance. (2) A matching OC-side per-reaction ledger (built by tracing KarrLedgerReplayStream's own draw index around every _sample_reaction_coords call). Both ledgers agreed on reaction gating, order, and draw count for 9 consecutive reactions (cumulative draws both 4) before the FIRST divergence, precisely isolated at iteration 10 (reaction index 26, WID DNADamage_THYTHY_cyclobutane_THYTHY_UVB_radiation, a 2-character string motif 'TT'): real MATLAB drew 24 raw values for this ONE reaction (both sides found n_sites_actual=1); OC drew only 23. Root cause (found, not merely triangulated): Chromosome.m::sampleAccessibleSites's real per-round break condition (`if size(positionsStrands,1) >= nSites: positionsStrands = this.randStream.randomlySelectNRows(positionsStrands, nSites); break; end`) calls randomlySelectNRows/randsample UNCONDITIONALLY whenever accumulated candidates reach (>=) the target -- INCLUDING the exact-match case (found precisely n_sites candidates, no actual selection ambiguity) -- because randsample(stream,n,n,false) with n==k still consumes n real draws (randsample.m's 4*k>n branch fires for any k>=1 when k==n, performing a full randperm(n) even though the output is merely a reordering of the same candidates). OC's opencell/vivarium/karr_dna_damage.py::_sample_literal_motif_sites used `if len(candidates) > n_sites` (strictly greater), silently SKIPPING this mandatory draw for the exact-match case -- fixed to `>=`. Two dedicated regression tests added in tests/vivarium/test_karr_dna_damage.py (test_sample_literal_motif_sites_draws_final_select_when_candidates_exactly_equal_n_sites, an exact-match-case unit test using a hand-crafted KarrLedgerReplayStream and an all-'A' synthetic sequence to force a controlled, reproducible exact-match scenario; plus an inversion test proving the prior `>` guard leaves the stream desynchronized). RESULT: rebuilding the OC-side per-reaction ledger after the fix shows FULL agreement with the real MATLAB ledger across all 32 of tick4's reactions -- same reaction order, same draw count per reaction (including the now-matching 24 for reaction 26), same cumulative draw count at every step, same final n_sites_actual -- zero divergence anywhere in the tick. The dedicated seed2000 test (renamed test_karr_dna_damage_l2_event_replay_seed2000_chromosome_ledger, xfail(strict=True) marker REMOVED, now a genuine unconditional PASS) replays the FULL 20-tick seed2000 window end-to-end with the ledger injected every tick and passes cleanly -- true bit identity for the entire window, not just tick 4. Re-ran the 55-trace L2.2 corpus verifier after this fix (applies process-wide, not just to ledgered traces): n_events_karr=99 (unchanged corpus), n_events_oc changed 90->84 (the fix altered which reactions/sites get selected across the corpus, as expected since draw-count desync from this bug would have propagated through every subsequent draw in an affected tick), joint_verdict remains PASS. Strict L2.1 rubric re-verified 14/14 passed, no regression to any other process. IMPORTANT DISCLOSURE on manifest classification: this manifest row's `classification` remains CODE_GAP and is NOT promoted to GENUINE, despite the algorithmic bug now being fully fixed and genuine bit identity proven for the complete 20-tick window. This is because the STANDARD, mechanical `l21_active_window_audit.py`/`verify_active_window_manifest_row` harness -- the tool this project consistently uses as the authoritative source for GENUINE/CODE_GAP determinations -- constructs a FRESH, non-ledgered KarrDNADamageProcess (the pre-existing, disclosed 'stand-in stream' architecture) and therefore cannot itself observe the ledger-driven bit identity this session established; re-running it after this fix reproduces the IDENTICAL first_mismatch_tick=4/oc_val=0.0/karr_val=1.0 divergence as before the fix (mechanically re-verified, verification_status=VERIFIED_CODE_GAP, fresh_classification=CODE_GAP matching recorded_classification), because a freshly-seeded, non-ledgered stream's specific stochastic outcome is uncorrelated with Karr's real interleaved-shared-stream position regardless of how correct the underlying selection algorithm now is. Promoting this row to GENUINE would require either (a) extending the shared, multi-process audit harness itself to support ledger injection (out of scope for a single-process RNG-fidelity fix; a larger, riskier change touching infrastructure used by every other process's L2.1 audit), or (b) accepting a documented exception to the harness's own classification for this one process. Neither was done here; the mechanical tool's own verdict is reported faithfully rather than overridden. The genuine, ledger-verified bit-identity result is fully documented here and in the passing test suite as the authoritative technical closure of this task's RNG-fidelity scope.
